summary.headline: MOFSL Q1FY27 operating PAT rose 14% YoY to ₹609 crore, led by Asset and Private Wealth businesses up 44% YoY.
summary.overview: Motilal Oswal reported Q1FY27 operating PAT of ₹609 crore, up 14% YoY, with Asset and Private Wealth Management contributing 55% of group operating PAT versus 50% in FY26. AMC AUM including MO alternates crossed ₹2 lakh crore and total AUM reached ₹4.5 lakh crore (up 34% YoY), with net flows of ₹10,325 crore. Wealth Management TBR revenue fell sharply on a high base, while ARR revenue grew 26% YoY to ₹304 crore. Management guided to lumpy capital markets execution, steady carry income accrual of around ₹66 crore per quarter, and a tailwind from maturing mutual fund vintages.

segments.name: Asset Management (AMC incl. MO alternates)
segments.commentary: AUM crossed ₹2 lakh crore with average AUM of ₹1.81 lakh crore in Q1FY27 vs ₹1.67 lakh crore in Q4FY26. Net MF flow market share 4.2% vs 3.7% in prior quarter; SIP flows ₹4,064 crore (+16% YoY, 4.3% share). Alternates net flow was negative for the quarter on gross inflows that were among the highest in the street; management says it is tracking net positive in July.

segments.name: Private Wealth Management
segments.commentary: AUM ₹2.4 lakh crore (+37% YoY), net flows nearly ₹4,000 crore (+37%), ARR AUM about ₹52,000 crore, 441 RMs. TBR revenue fell on a high base; NII on lending book of ₹4,200 crore is classified as ARR.

segments.name: Wealth Management (distribution, broking, lending)
segments.commentary: Distribution book grew nearly 30% to over ₹45,000 crore, with distribution yield stable at about 70 bps. Lending book up 33% YoY to over ₹7,000 crore; MTF market share near 6.5%. Overall retail broking share 7.6% incl. commodities, F&O premium share up from 7% to 7.6%.

segments.name: Capital Markets (Institutional Equities and IB)
segments.commentary: 11 IB deals completed in the quarter raising over ₹10,000 crore; company ranked #2 in IPO and QIP league tables. Equities coverage rose to 384 stocks after 20 initiations, with a target of 500.

segments.name: Housing Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹646 crore (+64% YoY) and AUM ₹6,164 crore (+23% YoY). Credit cost rose to about 1% in Q1 from 10 bps in Q4 on seasonal factors; FY26 credit cost was 0.5%.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Treasury book ₹10,482 crore (+22% YoY), with management citing a long-term compounded growth of about 40%, roughly 20% from IRR and the rest from reinvested operating profit.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capital markets revenue expected to grow overall, with execution concentrated in 2-3 windows of 2-3 months each; QoQ outcomes depend on market conditions, and a reasonable YoY growth is expected.

Unlisted alternates accrued variable additional return (carry) of about ₹66 crore per quarter, expected at similar levels for the next three quarters and higher next year; only about 70% of fair value is recognised.
Cost of borrowing expected to fall by 15-20 bps over the next 12-18 months following the CRISIL AA+ rating upgrade; capital market spreads have narrowed from 75 bps to 30-35 bps vs AAA peers.
Group operating margins (PBT) expected to sustain around 50-52% range, with about 70% of Wealth Management costs variable.

AMC: 4-5 new active fund offers over the next 12 months plus more passive offerings; private credit fund final close of ₹3,000 crore targeted in Q2 (about ₹2,500 crore raised); commercial real estate fund launch in H2 FY27.
Private Wealth RM headcount growth to be lower in FY27 than FY26 but with higher cost per RM targeted at family offices.
capex_capacity: Housing finance: management says the business has adequate capital adequacy and low leverage to grow without further capital infusion over the next 2-3 years.
Commercial real estate alternates fund approved by regulator; launch expected in H2 FY27.
Equities research coverage at 384 stocks, targeted to reach 500.
Three mutual fund schemes (small cap, large cap, multi-cap) crossing 3-year vintage between Dec 2026 and early 2027, with 2 more funds crossing by March 2027 and 8 more by March 2028.
Private Wealth RM count at 441; only 32% have over 3 years of vintage.
demand_pricing: Current AUM of nearly ₹1.9 lakh crore is over 15% above FY26 average AUM of ₹1.57 lakh crore, per management.
SIP run-rate per management: around ₹16,000 crore annualised; SIP AUM ₹38,643 crore; digital channel market share rose from about 6% in Q1FY26 to about 7%.

Alternates: private credit fund raised net ₹800 crore in Q1, with residual flows expected in Q2; competition from structured debt, private credit and real assets products pulled allocations from ultra-HNI clients.
Private Wealth wallet per client nearing ₹25 crore; AUM per banker near ₹550 crore; new-client flows about 20% of net flows.
MTF: management estimates about 15% of cash customers use MTF; MTF book grew 54% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Wealth Management distribution revenue fall 50% YoY while distribution assets grew 13%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a high TBR base in Q1FY26, led by unlisted revenues; distribution income is expected to track distribution assets from here, and TBR will be volatile QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HFC credit cost rise from 10 bps to about 1% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 typically sees higher 1+, 30+ and 90+ DPD numbers. FY26 credit cost was 0.5%, and management expects correction over the full year; GNPA is 1.1% vs 1.4% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Will the treasury book be affected by July volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said long-term compounded growth of about 40% since March 2014 is intact, though monthly or weekly figures can be volatile.

qa_highlights.question: Will alternates net flows recover and will carry income be booked?
qa_highlights.answer: Alternates saw negative net flows in Q1 due to market allocation shifts despite high gross inflows; July is tracking net positive. Listed equity carry was negligible; unlisted carry was ₹66 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will AMC and PWM PAT growth of 45% combined split out?
qa_highlights.answer: PWM PAT was up 2% due to lower TBR, so growth came from AMC, helped by the higher AUM base and accrued unlisted carry that started from Q3FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee expenses rise 16% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly annual appraisal and increments effective 1 April 2026; AMC had a one-time ESOP reversal in Q4FY26, so Q1 is a normalised base for the group going forward.

risks_watch: TBR revenue volatility in Private Wealth and Wealth Management, given high Q1FY26 base and unlisted-linked mix.
Capital markets revenue lumpiness dependent on market windows amid West Asia volatility.
Alternates net flows turned negative in Q1 as allocation shifted to competing credit and real-asset products; watch July-September net flow trend.
Impact of the 1 July 2026 prop trading regulatory change on broking and intraday funding, which management called minor but early to assess.
HFC credit cost trajectory during FY27 versus the FY26 level of 0.5%.
Mutual fund SIP market share has been range-bound; watch the 3-year vintage transition of key schemes from December 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on structural growth in AMC, alternates and annuity revenues, but cautious on capital markets and treasury timing, which management repeatedly called volatile and dependent on market windows. Management was candid that TBR and alternates flows were soft in the quarter and attributed them to the high base and market conditions.
key_quotes: We have transitioned from a transaction-led to an annuity-led business model, further strengthening the quality and sustainability of our earnings
Hence, FY27 as a whole, we'll witness growth. However, on a QoQ basis, it really depends on market.
The Asset Management business contributes to 40% of the group's operating PAT in Q1FY27 versus 26% in Q1FY26 and is expected to increase based on all the pointers highlighted above.
The entire Net Interest Income is ARR. There is no transactional in it.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 capital markets revenue to grow overall with a reasonable YoY growth, group PBT margin held at 50-52%, and ~₹66 crore per quarter of carry accrual for the next three quarters; backing is partly concrete (AUM ~₹1.9 lakh crore, 4-5 new fund offers, ₹2,500 crore raised toward ₹3,000 crore private credit close) but there is no quantified revenue growth target.
